newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Cepsa sees 6.5 bln pta Q1 profit.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Cepsa sees 6.5 bln pta Q1 profit.

text.p: Spanish energy group Cepsa expects to post first-quarter group net profits of about 6.5 billion pesetas ($44.9 million), chairman Carlos Perez de Bricio told reporters on Tuesday.
"We are not expecting to increase debt...in fact we are expecting to halve debt in the next four years," Perez de Bricio said. Cepsa's current financial debt is 140 billion pesetas.
In the first quarter of 1996, Cepsa posted net profit of 4.62 billion pesetas.
The chairman added that the firm plans to invest around 40 billion pesetas this year, versus 1996's record figure of 60 billion.
These investments will follow the same strategy as in the past, that is to improve and modernise chemical plants and refineries and to increase chemical production, he said.

With regard to Cepsa's entry into the domestic butane market, providing competition for Repsol, Perez de Bricio said: "We cannot be too ambitious given that there is a monopoly, but when we enter this area we're aiming for a market share of 15 percent."
He said that an agreement with Endesa to enter into the gas distribution business was still pending clarification from Brussels on the liberalisation of the Spanish market.
